summary: Final FLIPR 2026 gubernatorial forecast landing page as of Nov. 3, 2026. Democrats had a 90.2 percent chance of controlling a majority of governorships, Republicans 4.0 percent and a tie 5.8 percent. A projected 231.2 million Americans would have Democratic governors versus 111.3 million Republican. The PDF shows governor polling averages with per-poll influence scores; the Kansas average was tied at 48.3 each.

findings.statement: Final FLIPR gubernatorial aggregates on Nov. 3, 2026: Democrats 90.2 percent to hold a majority of governorships, Republicans 4.0 percent, tie 5.8 percent. Projected population governed: 231.2 million under Democrats and 111.3 million under Republicans.

Final Kansas governor polling average influence scores: AtlasIntel (2,038 LV, Oct 28-Nov 1) 3.25; NYT/Siena (736 LV) 2.37; YouGov (2,085 LV) 1.96; Emerson (800 LV) 1.92; Washington Post (801 LV) 1.81; Survey 160 (1,267 LV) 1.76; SSRS (838 LV, Oct 20-26) 1.02; Global Strategy Group, a Democratic partisan pollster (600 LV), 0.79; co/efficient (Sept 8-10) 0.11; YouGov (Sept 24-Oct 4) 0.10. Weights decay steeply with age once newer polls exist.
FLIPR's poll tables only display races with at least three polls from two unique polling firms, and label samples LV, RV, V or A.
